body:
Epic. Introduce **admin users** and a server-wide settings surface. Admin status
is assignable ONLY server-side (server config + CLI) — never through any
in-app/API path, so there is no privilege-escalation route. Admins get an extra
"Server" tab (web + android) for instance-wide configuration.

## First cut — three capabilities

1. **Enable/disable registration at runtime.** The server-config default
   (`allow_registration`, T-61) still applies at startup, but an admin may
   override it live, and the override persists across restarts (until changed).
2. **Reset a user's password.** Admin-triggered, for users who lost theirs —
   the server side already exists (`accounts.reset_password(conn, email)`,
   generates a new password + revokes all that account's sessions; today only
   reachable via the `reset-password` CLI).
3. **Delete a user.** Admin-triggered removal of an account and all its data.
   `accounts.delete_account` exists but requires the account's own password;
   this needs an admin variant that deletes by id without it.

## Design notes / where this touches the codebase

**Admin identity (no in-app assignment).**
- Schema: add `accounts.is_admin INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (schema.sql +
  migration 4 — this will be the 2nd migration exercised after T-104's #3).
- CLI: `grant-admin <email>` / `revoke-admin <email>` (mirror the existing
  `reset-password` command shape, `_instance_option` for multi-mount).
- Server config: also accept an admin-email allowlist in server config (env/
  create_blueprint arg) applied at startup, so a fresh deploy can bootstrap its
  first admin without a manual CLI step. Config + CLI are the ONLY writers.
- Invariant to enforce and test: no API endpoint can set is_admin. Consider
  refusing to delete/demote the last remaining admin.

**Runtime-overridable server settings need persistence.**
- `allow_registration` is currently startup-only in-memory per-instance config
  (`get_config()`); a runtime override must be stored in the DB. Add a small
  persisted server-settings store (e.g. a `server_settings` key/value table, or
  columns on the existing single-row `meta` table) keyed per database/instance.
- Precedence: runtime override if present, else the startup config default.
- WRINKLE: the web client's register option is baked into the served index.html
  at startup as `<meta name="app-allow-registration">` (webapp.py
  `_transformed_index`). A runtime toggle won't be reflected by that static meta
  tag. The register *route* already re-checks config per request (auth.py), so
  the enforcement is fine — but the client's shown/hidden register UI would go
  stale. Fix: serve the effective flag from a small runtime endpoint the client
  reads (e.g. fold into an existing bootstrap/settings fetch) instead of / in
  addition to the baked meta tag.

**Admin API surface (all behind an `admin_required` gate on `g.account`).**
- `GET /admin/users` — list accounts (email, created_at, is_admin, session
  count) to act on.
- `GET/PUT /admin/server-settings` — read/set the registration override.
- `POST /admin/users/<id>/reset-password` — returns the generated password once
  (admin relays it out-of-band, same trust model as invite tokens; the server
  sends no email).
- `DELETE /admin/users/<id>` — delete a user (guard: not the last admin; decide
  whether an admin may delete themselves here vs. only via self-service).

**Clients.**
- Server must tell the client whether the current account is admin (add
  `is_admin` to the login response and/or GET /settings). The extra tab renders
  only when true.
- Web: new page/tab in SettingsPage or a sibling route; reuse the existing
  form/status patterns.
- Android: new Compose screen + ViewModel, gated in navigation on the admin flag.

**Cross-cutting.**
- Admin actions are sensitive — consider minimal audit logging (who did what,
  when). Can be a fast-follow, but note it now.
- Account enumeration: `GET /admin/users` deliberately exposes the full list,
  which is fine (admin-only) but should never be reachable unauthenticated or by
  a non-admin — cover with tests.
- Multi-instance: admin and server-settings are per-database/per-instance;
  document that an admin on tenant A is not an admin on tenant B.

## Suggested breakdown when picked up (probably split into sub-tickets)
1. Schema + migration + CLI grant/revoke + config allowlist + `admin_required`.
2. Persisted server-settings store + runtime registration override + client flag
   plumbing (fix the stale meta-tag path).
3. Admin API endpoints (users list, reset password, delete user).
4. Web admin tab.
5. Android admin tab.

Not started per instruction — filed for a future batch.
title: Admin users + server-wide settings tab (registration toggle, reset password, delete user)
